_comment: Cloud bot: HourlyTrend on Gate.io, dry-run only, no API keys. Gate.io rather than Bybit because Bybit and Binance both refuse GitHub's runners (403 / 451) - see research/make_cloud_config_gate.py. Prices differ from Bybit's by a fraction of a percent on liquid coins, which is acceptable for a paper test. Live trading would still need Bybit.
_comment_order_types: Stated explicitly rather than inherited, so no comment anywhere can contradict what actually runs. These ARE freqtrade's defaults - nothing about execution changes by writing them down - but the previous config left them implicit while a comment described market orders, and the two disagreed for weeks. KNOWN TRADEOFF, left alone deliberately: stoploss is a LIMIT order, so in a violent move it can fail to fill and the position outlives its stop. Market would be safer, and would also change fill prices versus every backtest run so far, so it is a decision to make with a measurement rather than a silent edit. stoploss_on_exchange stays FALSE: Gate supports it (freqtrade Gate._ft_has) but it is a no-op in dry-run, where freqtrade simulates the order and only checks it while the bot is actually iterating.

entry_pricing._comment_price_side: MUST be "other". CORRECTED 2026-08-29: this previously claimed the strategy uses "freqtrade's default MARKET orders". That is false - freqtrade's defaults are {entry: limit, exit: limit, stoploss: limit}, verified against IStrategy.order_types. The setting is still right, for a different reason: "other" prices the LIMIT order at the far side of the book (a buy at the ask), which crosses the spread and fills immediately, so the paper account PAYS the spread. With "same" it priced entries at the bid and exits at the ask, EARNING the spread twice per round trip and flattering the result. freqtrade validates this (config_validation._validate_price_config) but only after the strategy is resolved, so 'trade' and 'backtesting' never raised it - 'lookahead-analysis' did. Backtesting is unaffected either way: it fills from candle prices, not the order book.

_comment_api_server: Added 2026-08-31 so Telegram can CLOSE a trade. This is the only way anything outside freqtrade changes a position, and that is deliberate: writing 'closed' into the sqlite file under a running bot leaves freqtrade's memory and the database disagreeing about what is open - it would go on managing a stop for a trade that no longer exists and rewrite the row on its next iteration. Through the API, freqtrade places the exit order itself. Bound to 127.0.0.1, so it is reachable only from inside the GitHub runner; there is no public port, and no exchange key exists on that machine in any case. The username below is real. The password and jwt_secret_key are PLACEHOLDERS - the workflow overrides both per run via FREQTRADE__API_SERVER__PASSWORD and FREQTRADE__API_SERVER__JWT_SECRET_KEY, generated fresh each job with openssl, so no usable credential is ever committed. They are spelled out here rather than left blank because freqtrade's schema requires all six keys to be present and jwt_secret_key to be at least 32 characters; a blank value fails config validation before an env override could rescue it.
